questions.q: Harrow has three sales segments with different stage names and required fields, but leadership wants one combined pipeline report across all three. What does this combination point toward?
options: One Opportunity object with a record type per segment
Three separate Salesforce orgs, one per segment
Three separate Opportunity objects, one per segment
Deleting the Stage field entirely so no segment has required fields
questions.explain: Different processes on the same object, needed in one combined report, is exactly the case record types solve: each segment gets its own stages, required fields, and layout, while all three stay in one Opportunity object that a single report type can roll up.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend starting Harrow's Opportunity OWD at Private rather than a more open setting?
options: Private is required for any object that has record types
Widening OWD later is comparatively low-risk, while tightening it later forces re-auditing every sharing mechanism built on top of the looser default
Record types cannot function unless OWD is Private
Sales reps are not allowed to see their own records under any other setting
questions.explain: Starting with the more restrictive OWD is the safer direction specifically because loosening it later is low-risk, while tightening it later is a breaking change that forces re-examining every sharing rule and manual share built on the old default.

questions.q: Enterprise reps' account-team visibility was handled by ad hoc manual sharing, which kept getting forgotten. What should replace it?
options: A new record type with a different sharing setting
Raising OWD to Public Read/Write for everyone
A criteria-based sharing rule tied to the enterprise account-team flag
Nothing — manual sharing is the only mechanism that can grant team-based access
questions.explain: A criteria-based sharing rule automates exactly the grant reps were trying to make manually and forgetting — it fires whenever a record matches the account-team flag, without depending on anyone remembering to click share.

questions.q: Role hierarchy automatically grants which kind of visibility in Harrow's design?
options: A rep can see deals owned by reps in a completely unrelated role
Every rep can see every other rep's deals regardless of segment
Only the org admin can see any Opportunity record
A rep's manager can see the records owned by the reps below them in the hierarchy
questions.explain: Role hierarchy's specific behavior is upward visibility: records owned by someone lower in the hierarchy become visible to the roles above them, which is why each segment's manager gets visibility into their own team automatically, without extra configuration.

questions.q: Before Harrow's record-type design ships, what specific reporting risk needs to be checked and not just assumed?
options: That each record type's differently-named stages are correctly mapped to the right underlying forecast category so revenue rolls up correctly
That every segment uses the exact same stage names
That record types are disabled on the Opportunity object
That the VP of Sales personally approves each individual deal
questions.explain: Different record types can use different display names for their stages, but those stages still have to map to the correct forecast category (Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed) for forecasting and rollups to work — an unmapped or mismapped stage silently drops or miscounts revenue, which is exactly the kind of check that has to happen before launch.
